chunks: Which had left you devoid of hope,

key_terms.ظَهْرَکَ: your back (metaphorically: your strength, hope, or posture)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when the Quran says 'Which had left you devoid of hope'?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this phrase from Surah Yusuf (12:87) is interpreted as the profound emotional strain borne by Prophet Yaqub (Jacob) while awaiting the return of his sons, symbolizing the 'breaking of one's back' through intense longing and patience (sabr). It underscores the human reality of spiritual fatigue even for the infallible Imams, validating the expression of grief as a legitimate component of devotion and reliance on divine timing.
